sub_answers.sub_question: What provisions related to provincial powers are contained in Sri Lanka's Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution?
sub_answers.text: The Thirteenth Amendment provides for devolution of power to the provinces and established a new system of provincial government through the Provincial Councils Act No 42 of 1987 [d81740317s2p0]. The amendment enabled a proposed merger of the Northern and Eastern provinces subject to a later referendum [d225283s3p0]. The amendment gave official status to the Tamil language as part of its concessions to Tamil demands [d225283s3p0]. The amendment was enacted alongside a commitment that Sri Lankan troops would be confined to barracks in the Northern and Eastern provinces as part of the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord arrangements [d81740317s2p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which Sri Lankan political parties and Tamil groups have advocated for greater regional autonomy or federal arrangements for the Northern Province?
sub_answers.text: Tamil militant groups including the LTTE, TELO, PLOTE, EROS, EPRLF and TELA were active parties in the struggle over autonomy and sought greater self-determination for Tamils in the north and east [d225283s3p0]. Tamil nationalist political leaders initially welcomed the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord and the devolution measures it contained [d81740317s2p0]. The LTTE attempted to create an independent Tamil state called Tamil Eelam, reflecting advocacy for maximal regional autonomy or separation by some Tamil groups [d6033791s5p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the specific constitutional provisions, articles and schedules in Sri Lanka's Thirteenth Amendment that define provincial powers, including subjects devolved to provincial councils, financial arrangements, the establishment of a Provincial Council, and any limits or reserved powers retained by the central government.
sub_answers.text: The Indo‑Sri Lanka Accord led to the Sri Lankan Government passing the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution and the Provincial Councils Act No. 42 of 1987 on 14 November 1987 to establish a new system of provincial government with the aim of devolution of power to the provinces.[d81740317s2p0] The Provincial Councils Act No. 42 of 1987 and the Thirteenth Amendment together established provincial councils as the institutional vehicle for devolution.[d81740317s2p0] A governor may appoint a chief minister who, in his opinion, commands the support of a majority of the provincial council.[d18577075s1p0] Chief ministers are elected heads of the provincial boards of ministers that aid and advise the governors in the exercise of their executive power.[d18577075s0p0]

The LTTE sought to create an independent Tamil state called Tamil Eelam in the northeast of Sri Lanka, which affected governance and control of territories in the Northern Province during the civil war period [d6033791s5p0].
